main_issue: Corrupt block in a deposited chain, and four dropped minus signs
finding: Table 4 recounted from the 22.4 GB of MCMC chains the collaboration deposited, not a re-run of the inference. The paper states its estimator in an appendix — the Bayes estimator is the sample mean of the 1D marginal and its standard deviation the sample standard deviation — which is the sentence our DES Y3 rerun found missing, and it makes the recount well posed. 103 of the 112 Bayes-estimator cells come back from the deposited arrays with no burn-in and no thinning; 108 once each cell is scored at the precision it is actually printed to. Four things in the remainder. One deposited file, sigw_gauss_bhb.pkl.gz, ends in a contiguous block of 46,378 corrupt rows (indices 2,788,847 to 2,835,224, finishing on the last row) whose log_posterior runs from 1.5e7 to 1.3e12, where the clean part of that same file tops out at 8.8e6 and the other 29 files sit within about ten of 7.9728e6; in those rows gamma_bhb reaches 13.53 against a largest value of 6.45 anywhere else. Remove exactly those rows and the model's published values return — gamma_BHB 4.6542 ± 0.3441 against a printed 4.65 ± 0.34, where the full file gives 4.7993 ± 1.1759. The paper is right and the deposited file is not, and nothing in the deposit flags it. Three cells print log10 alpha_* with the sign reversed: pt-bubble NP −0.26 against our +0.2634, pt-bubble NP+SMBHB −0.23 against +0.2256, pt-sound NP −0.22 against +0.2187, each with the standard deviation printed in the same cell reproducing exactly. The fourth cell of that parameter prints +0.14 and reproduces, so it is not a convention between chains and table, and dw-sm's alpha_* is genuinely −0.88 and reproduces as printed. In the two pt-bubble rows the table is at odds with itself, printing a maximum posterior of 1* and an interval of [0.03, 1*] beside a negative mean. A fourth sign is dropped in the dw-dr ΔN_eff interval, and that one is visible from the paper alone: the NP+SMBHB column prints an upper edge of 0.41*, the asterisk means by the caption that the value sits at the prior boundary, and Table 3 gives that prior as log-uniform on [−3, −0.41]; the NP column of the same row prints −0.41. One cell we could not account for: Δ in sigw-gauss comes out at 1.30505 after the corrupt rows go, against a printed 1.30, and both ways of cutting those rows give the same answer. The Bayes factors, including the 10 to 100 favouring cosmological models over black-hole binaries, are out of scope throughout: they come from the evidence, not the marginals. A blind recount with its own pre-registration, frozen before it opened a chain and with no sight of our scripts or results, reached the first two findings independently and supplied the third; it also scored the interval column and showed the printed intervals are genuine highest-density regions, median coverage 0.6806 over 112 of them. Our own adversarial review then corrected the headline count, which had been 108 by counting a cell that fails and failing a cell that passes, and took out two comparison figures that flattered the case.

main_issue: Group labels swapped in the figure script
finding: The young-vs-old comparison of Figure 4BI, from the authors' own OSF deposit and their own config: one 8-state TDE-HMM trained on the 65-subject MEG release, then stats.group_diff with 1000 permutations and the max statistic, as the paper describes. The effects reproduce and the directions do not. Fractional occupancy of the sensorimotor network comes out 0.1556 in the young group against 0.1239 in the old (p = 0.022 to 0.029), its switching rate 2.4442 against 1.9676 (p = 0.033 to 0.038), and the mean lifetime of the visual network 0.0602 against 0.0672 (p = 0.032 to 0.033) — the same metrics and the same networks the text names, each with the sign the text gives reversed. The networks were identified from the per-parcel PSD over each state's Viterbi path, not from the state index, since HMM numbering is arbitrary per fit. The cause is one line of examples/toolbox_paper/ctf_rest/tde_hmm_networks.py, the script the caption of Figure 4 links to by URL: group = ["Old" if a == 1 else "Young" for a in assignments], where load_group_assignments just above builds 1 for young and 2 for old. The list feeds only the seaborn hue, so the p-values are untouched and the legend is swapped; tde_dynemo_networks.py carries the same line. Three things tie it to the printed figure: the caption's own link, the deposited model reporting osl-dynamics version: 2.0.dev3 against a line present at v2.0.0, and the colour order being derivable — seaborn orders hue by first appearance, subject00 is 39, so "Young" is level 0 and therefore blue, which is what the published legend shows. On every starred panel the violin labelled "Young" sits at our old group's median (0.1214, 1.8932, 1.3968, 0.8395) and the long mean-interval tails labelled "Old" run into the range of our young group's longest intervals. A control with no model in it settles which group is which: static sensorimotor beta power straight from the parcel time courses gives young 0.1428 against old 0.1815, p = 0.00086, r with age +0.43 — the known ageing effect, and the same direction the authors' own Figure 6 reports under the opposite group coding that static_networks.py uses on purpose (old = 1, if a < 34). Two conventions for the same two groups in one folder. This matters past the legend: section 2.5 links the static beta increase to "a larger fraction of time spent in the sensorimotor network", and as measured static beta rises with age while that network's occupancy falls (r = −0.38). Three more things about the deposit. The trained TDE-HMM it ships for the paper's own parcellation is n_states: 12 where the script trains 8 and the figure shows 8, and it omits pca_components.npy, so its covariances cannot be mapped back onto the data — re-deriving the PCA recovers the subspace (60 of 80 principal-angle cosines above 0.99) but not the basis within it (median absolute cosine per component 0.15). The only 8-state inferred parameters cover 5 subjects of 65. And the DyNeMo archive holds covariances of shape (20, 6, 80, 80) — six modes, where the script sets n_modes: 7 and the text analyses the 7-mode fit — with no weights and no mode time courses, so those claims cannot be recomputed at all; Figure 5BI is legible as swapped the same way. The group sizes reproduce exactly, 27 and 38 of 65 under the authors' age > 34 rule, but the printed age ranges do not describe the sample: demographics.csv holds seven banded values and the realised groups are 21–33 and 39–60, with nobody at 34. A blind recount with its own pre-registration, frozen before it computed anything and with no access to ours, reached the label swap on its own and corrected us on the way: our first pass printed the contrast as old-young when group_diff returns Group_1 − Group_2 and group 1 is the young one — the same class of error, in our code, caught by a disagreement on sign. Our adversarial review then took out three things the draft claimed: that the violins match to three decimals (they do not; medians are the honest comparison), that the two runs were four independent fits (both called set_random_seed(1) and produced the identical model, free energy 110.20281682757752 — three fits, not four), and that the same states come out significant (true for 3 of 5 cells, and our fit has a sixth near threshold that the figure does not star).

main_issue: Interval definition in the paper is not the one printed
finding: Recount of the published posterior summaries from the chains the collaboration deposited, not a re-run of the PolyChord inference. All ten central values come back to the last printed digit — S_8 = 0.7760 against 0.776 and Ω_m = 0.3388 against 0.339 in ΛCDM, w = −0.9808 against −0.98, and the combined-probe S_8 = 0.8120 and h = 0.6802 against 0.812 and 0.680. Four of the bounds miss our frozen rule, and they miss because the rule was wrong: we froze 16th/84th percentiles, and the published bounds are the 68% highest-density interval of the smoothed marginal, which reproduces all twenty. The percentile reading a reader would reach for gives w = −0.98 ± 0.27 against the printed +0.32 −0.20, losing the asymmetry that carries the physics. Two things to report. The paper defines the interval exactly once, in Section V — "the mean in each parameter, along with the 68% confidence limit (CL) of posterior volume around the mean" — and taken literally that recipe gives the asymmetry inverted: w comes out +0.23 −0.36 against the printed +0.32 −0.20, and σ_8 in ΛCDM +0.052 −0.040 against +0.039 −0.049. The highest-density interval does not use the mean at all, and the printed central value is not at its centre: for w the interval runs from −1.186 to −0.653 with the mean 38% of the way along. And read_chains_y3a2.py, shipped in the same folder as the chains, reads σ_8 at column index 30 and the weight at index 36, which is right only for a 37-column header; of the 29 chains in that folder, 3 are like that and the rest run 14 to 62 columns. On the fiducial 3x2pt ΛCDM chain it reads bias_ta as σ_8 and the log-posterior as the weight, returning a mean S_8 of 0.93 instead of 0.776 and raising no error; on the file the script itself opens, the offset is six and S_8 comes out at −0.42 against 0.849. Reading the header line instead of indexing is three lines of code. A blind recount with its own pre-registered list of candidate definitions reached the same rule independently, and supplied both the inversion and the six-column offset. Our own adversarial review caught a figure in the first draft that had been written from intuition and never computed: dropping the weight column moves S_8 by 0.052, not the 0.003 the draft claimed.

main_issue: Table column is not the quantity described
finding: Table S4 of the Supporting Information, the two RNNs the table names first: 100,000 sequences sampled from each pretrained model on CPU with the authors' own dev code, and the two ratios recomputed. One of our four frozen values lands inside the band. The reason the other three miss is that the validity column of the RNN rows is not validity: it is the share of sampled sequences that came out as a non-empty string, parseable or not. That rule reproduces the printed value on all twenty RNN machine-rows of the authors' own deposit and on both of our samples, while the share RDKit actually parses is 0.685 for the ChEMBL 27 LSTM against a printed 0.999, and 0.914 for the ChEMBL 31 GRU against 1.000. The row that settles it is the ChEMBL 27 LSTM, the only RNN not printing 1.000: its 0.999 is neither a rounded 1.000 nor a rounded 0.685, it is exactly what about ninety empty strings in 100,000 leave behind, and our run gives 80. The legend describes the parseable ratio, so as printed the column is near 1.000 for any model that emits a string at all. The ChEMBL 27 LSTM uniqueness of 0.600 we could not account for at all: the four readings we could build off the authors' deposited molecules give 0.661, 0.572, 0.594 and 0.390, and their own six machines print 0.599 to 0.601, so it is stable and not a slip. A blind recount with its own sample and its own pre-registered definitions reached the same four candidates and the same dead end, and no code in the release computes either column: generate() defaults to dropping invalids and duplicates and resampling until it holds the count, so its output is valid and unique by construction. Our sample and theirs are the same distribution: 51.5% of our distinct molecules appear in a single deposited machine of 100,000, against 51.9% between two of their own machines. Also, python -m drugex.generate fails on a default install, because generate.py imports drugex.train, which imports the optional qsprpred at module level.

main_issue: Scoring code penalises the baselines
finding: The segmentation benchmark of Extended Data Fig. 2a/b: volume regenerated with the authors' own generator, four of the thirteen noise levels segmented with Nellie 0.4.1, scored with their own check_IoU. On the 100-cell slice the figure exports, 6 of our 8 frozen values land inside the band, IoU within 0.011 of print at three of the four levels. Nine things do not line up, and two of them change the published comparison. The if len(unique_labels) < 100 guard in the scoring code skips the matching loop and scores the cell zero whatever the overlap: Nellie never reaches it at any level we ran, at most 63 labels in a cell, while Triangle reaches it in all 1000 cells at σ = 8192, up to 1113 labels, and the published Triangle row there is exactly 0.0000 ± 0.0000. We reproduce that zero and the 0.0396 one level up, where only 27 cells trip the guard, so the non-monotonic bump in the published curve is the guard switching off. And fp goes negative when one label fills the crop, which scores a correct match F1 = 0. Both can only cost a method that over-segments or saturates, never the one being evaluated. The Source Data prints N = 10 on every row and that is arithmetically impossible: F1 is bounded in [0, 1], so three rows print an sd above the largest ten values can have, and two of them reconstruct exactly as 100 cells. Also: the level axis is labelled intensity where the generator varies length; add_noise clips the noise instead of the frame, so the x axis sweeps a background offset of σ/√(2π) together with the noise; and the release ships a runner for every competing method but none for Nellie, sets no seed, and its two pin sets contradict each other, so the figure cannot be rebuilt from it. Two of our own numbers do not reproduce and we cannot attribute them, F1 0.3624 against 0.1300 at σ = 32768 and 0.9800 against a printed 1.0000 at σ = 8 — but Otsu and Triangle, sharing the same volume, ground truth, noise draw and scoring, come back to four decimals, 14 of 16 numbers within 0.0027, so whatever that difference is, it is in the segmenter.

Recount of the published posterior summaries from the EPTA DR2 chains on Zenodo, not a re-run of the Bayesian search. Across the fourteen ENTERPRISE cells of Table 2 and Table A.1, 25 of the 28 medians come back within 0.005 of print, so the chains and the tables are the same analysis. Three things do not line up. Table 2 gives the DR2new GWB spectral index a lower bound of −0.71, but the paper's own Section 4 and conclusions both print −0.73 and the chain gives −0.7322, so the table misprints one digit — and that single cell was the whole of our frozen failure. Table A.1 is captioned “90% credible regions” but all eight of its ENTERPRISE numbers match our 68% equal-tailed bounds to within 0.005, with the best-fitting level between 67.5% and 68.8% on every one, while the same scan puts Table 2 at exactly 90.0%; as printed, a reader comparing the two tables would read the InPTA addition as tightening the constraint by about 40%. And the three DR2new ORF rows of Table 2 match no standard level, best fit 85-87%, the binned row off by 0.157 on a bound and 0.022 on a median, while the same three chains in DR2full reproduce to within 0.005 — unexplained. The blind recount found the first of the three by reading the LaTeX source instead of the PDF; the adversarial review forced the survey that found the other two, after pointing out that the three frozen claims were the quiet corner of a release that supports fourteen cells.

Flat ΛCDM from the public DR2 BAO distances, our own likelihood and a dense marginalised grid with CAMB: Omega_m = 0.29755 ± 0.00863 against 0.2975 ± 0.0086, r_d h = 101.5313 ± 0.7360 Mpc against 101.54 ± 0.73, and H0 with BBN 68.5466 ± 0.5980 against 68.51 ± 0.58. All three inside the pre-registered band, the worst at 0.063σ. The DR1 prior defect does not repeat: refitting H0 under the slice DR1's chain imposed gives −0.223σ and under DR2's varying-N_eff prior −0.242σ, both outside the band, so only the prior the paper prints reproduces the paper's H0. Three things about the release: the released 13×13 covariance is not the likelihood of Table IV, being 0.2 to 11.5% wider along the isotropic direction while matching to 0.1-2.5% along the Alcock-Paczynski one; the Lyman-alpha row of the mean file lists D_H before D_M, the reverse of every other tracer; and the Lyman-alpha D_M/r_d of Table IV is truncated, not rounded. An independent blind rerun got the same three values. An adversarial review then found two false statements the report made about itself, both corrected and named in it: the grids were not pre-registered, and one frozen edge-mass gate was missed.

main_issue: Released test set differs from the paper counts
finding: The MAE block of Supporting Information Table S1, 42 numbers, with the three released MACE-OFF23 checkpoints and the SPICE test file on Apollo. Every value falls inside our pre-registered band, so by our rule it is reproduced; an independent blind rerun got the same 42 numbers, set a tighter band and calls it partially reproduced, 36 of 42. All 6 it fails are PubChem, and both runs trace that to the same cause: the released PubChem set has 209 more configurations than the count in Table 1. Removing configurations whose largest Cartesian reference force component exceeds 10 eV/Å reproduces the Table 1 counts exactly, 33,884 and 13,896, and then all 42 values round to the published ones. The paper does not mention that cut, and the senior author did not confirm it. On the five subsets whose size already matches Table 1, all 30 values round to the published number with no filtering at all. Run on a home RTX 2070 SUPER. The weights are under the Academic Software License and are not redistributed here; the authors gave permission for the report and scripts to be published.

main_issue: Source Data table corrupt on deposit
finding: Figure 4, base against fine-tuned model, 260 protein-organism pairs: Jaccard 0.7379 against 0.74 published, codon similarity 69.2629% against 69.26%, normalized DTW 0.0459 ± 0.0338 against 0.05 ± 0.03. The released checkpoints regenerate all 520 benchmark sequences byte for byte. An independent blind rerun got the same numbers to every digit and a different label, because the two runs set different bands: ours asked for 1e-6 agreement on each of 260 DTW values and got none, which fails our own frozen rule, while the blind run put its band on the means alone and passes. We publish both and name the bad band as ours. Three defects in the release: the per-pair DTW table of the Source Data carries one value per protein under every pair label, found independently by both runs; equation 6 of the Methods does not describe the %MinMax that was computed, which is the Clarke & Clark statistic the cited R package implements; and the base checkpoint repository ships no tokenizer. The paper's own figure is fine.

main_issue: Reference data offline or deleted
finding: From the released chains, no re-sampling: the HD amplitude at gamma = 13/3 comes out at 2.4039 (+0.665/−0.589) × 10⁻¹⁵, the authors' own stored output to the digit, and the thermodynamic-integration Bayes factors give log10 BF 12.11 (CURN vs IRN) and 14.41 (HD vs IRN), inside the published ranges. The chain behind the headline number was removed from the repository in 2024 and survives only in its git history and on Google Drive. Two smaller points: the presampled HD vs CURN core is a fixed-gamma run, not the varied-gamma comparison of Fig. 2, and the TI quadrature moves log10 BF by 0.3, more than the quoted ±0.1. An independent blind rerun got the same numbers.

main_issue: Code differs from the Methods
finding: Flat ΛCDM from the public DR1 BAO distances, our own likelihood with CAMB: Omega_m = 0.2947 ± 0.0146 against 0.295 ± 0.015 and r_d h = 101.90 ± 1.27 Mpc against 101.8 ± 1.3. H0 with BBN comes out at 68.69 ± 0.81 against 68.53 ± 0.80, 0.2σ high and just outside our band. The cause is in the authors' own chain: Section 2.4.1 gives the ΛCDM BBN prior as Eq. (2.8), but the chain behind the published H0 uses the ΛCDM+N_eff prior evaluated at N_eff = 3.044, which shifts the mean down by 0.37σ. Their chain that does use Eq. (2.8) gives 68.67, like ours. An independent blind rerun, by an agent with no access to the first one, reached the same values and found the same prior on its own.

main_issue: Test lists or evaluation commands not published
finding: Fig. 2b with the released weights: median ROC AUC 0.9247 against 0.92 on the 53 MaSIF-site subunits, and all 53 match the authors' own notebook outputs to three decimals. On the 417-structure ScanNet set, 0.9299 against 0.93, with 415 of 416 structures matching the Source Data to 0.001. Neither the benchmark dataset file nor the ScanNet structure list is in the repo, so we rebuilt both. Two entries drifted with PDB revisions: 4DX0 gives 0.961 instead of 0.909, and 1FSS now exceeds the code’s atom limit and drops out. An independent blind rerun, by an agent with no access to the first one, reached the same values.

main_issue: Released checkpoints differ from the paper
finding: Table 3 (scaffold splits) with the published fine-tuned weights: BBBP 0.8913 against 0.902, BACE 0.7104 against 0.832, Tox21 0.6131 against 0.653, SIDER 0.7180 against 0.745, and no model is published for the HIV column. Our validation run matches the authors' own TensorBoard logs, which ship inside the model folders, bit for bit on three metrics per task, so the split, the metric and the weights are theirs. The published scaffold training command also crashes as released, on the line that prints the number. An independent blind rerun, by an agent with no access to the first one, reached the same values.

main_issue: Code differs from the Methods
finding: Fig. 1 (global RMSE, 2020) for IFS HRES, GraphCast, Pangu-Weather, the two operational-start rows and NeuralGCM 0.7°: all 50 pre-registered Z500 and T850 cells match on the full 732 initialisations. Z500 matches with the public code as it is; T850 only matches with the below-ground mask of Section 4.2.1, which is not in the public code. We pointed the authors to it. We also reported that the 2026 benchmark files disagreed with the GraphCast stores by up to 0.58%; that was ours — the files come from the _v2 stores and we had evaluated the older ones. Re-run against graphcast_hres_init_v2 the five operational Z500 scores come back as 40.53334007, 124.41172879, 276.74144748, 477.17220428 and 754.01772109, which is the released file to every digit it prints. Corrected in the report on 2026-11-20.

main_issue: Settings behind one result not published
finding: Power Law + Peak run, rerun twice from the released event arrays and injections: mass peak 33.5-33.6 Msun (paper 34 +2.6/-4.0) and BBH rate at z=0.2 of 28.3-28.4 Gpc^-3 yr^-1 (paper 28.3 +13.9/-9.1). The rate step reuses a stale spin shape, which moves the median by about 0.13, and the example config differs from the published run.

main_issue: Reference data re-released
finding: Table 1 (compleasm rows) with the v0.2.2 release: six of seven genomes agree within 0.3 points on every category. Maize gives 99.4% complete against 96.7% with today's BUSCO odb10 lineage, re-released in 2024. With the 2020 lineage the author sent us, maize matches too: 96.72 complete, 82.23 single, 14.49 duplicated, 3.03 fragmented. v0.2.2 also crashes on today's lineage index.

main_issue: Released checkpoints differ from the paper
finding: 2022 tables with the 2022 data and checkpoints: 21 of 26 nRMSE values match at the printed 2 significant figures, including all 10 Darcy Flow values. The released 2022 Advection β=1.0 FNO checkpoint behaves like a β=0.4 model (nRMSE 0.63 against 5.9e-03), and three Burgers FNOs come out 1-9% lower. We told the authors.

main_issue: Reference data offline or deleted
finding: Fig. 2B (AFDB clusters): on the 32 clusters whose inputs are still complete, 31 give the authors' LDDT to 6 decimals and the same alignment. 285 of the 3,200 benchmark structures have since been deleted from AlphaFold DB, so the 160-cluster means run on reduced inputs only. Fig. 2A could not run: the HOMSTRAD reference is offline and not archived anywhere we could find.

main_issue: Code differs from the Methods
finding: Fig. 4 (ligand-receptor methods scored against spatial co-localisation on 5 Slide-tags datasets) re-runs from the released files and matches the Source Data to about 1e-16. In the evaluation code, the FDR correction the Methods describe is applied to a 0/1 vector and has no effect; done as described, it reorders the methods. We asked which was intended.

main_issue: Settings behind one result not published
finding: Table 3 with the released distances and covariance: Omega_m = 0.3327 ± 0.018 against 0.334 ± 0.018 in flat ΛCDM; the ΛCDM and wCDM rows and the SH0ES H0 (73.54 against 73.6) also hold. The w0waCDM row does not (Omega_m 0.32 against 0.403); it depends on the prior range, and the authors' released chains do not reach 0.403 either. We asked which prior and settings produced it.

main_issue: New dependency release breaks results
finding: Table 1 with the released checkpoints on all 20 M JetClass test jets: ParT accuracy 0.86051 and AUC 0.98772 match the printed 0.861 and 0.9877, and all nine background rejections fall inside the pre-registered statistical band; all 11 ParticleNet numbers match. The README installs weaver-core>=0.4, which now gives 0.5.3; with it the same checkpoint runs without error but scores 0.123 accuracy.

main_issue: Test lists or evaluation commands not published
finding: Table 1 (protein-to-genome alignment accuracy of miniprot-0.7): % confirmed splice junctions matches in all four columns, but base-level sensitivity on the human genome comes out 0.95 to 1.2 points lower and 6 of 12 percentages miss the 0.5-point tolerance. The paper does not publish the test protein lists or the evaluation command lines; we asked the author for both.

main_issue: Numbers differ, cause unknown
finding: Fig. 4 (COMP6 energy and force errors of three released ML potentials) does not reproduce: 3 of 36 values match, the rest differ in both directions. Two independent runs of ours agree with each other within 0.03 meV/atom. The model ranking holds. We asked the authors how the figure was computed.

main_issue: Code differs from the Methods
finding: All five headline numbers (ESM-1b and four ESM2 sizes) match within 0.003 over all 217 assays, confirmed by a second, independent run. The paper's averages come from the script's protein-first grouping, not the text's definition; ESM-1b was scored with wt-marginals, not the masked-marginals the appendix states; and five long-protein ESM2 scores were computed on the MSA region only, unlike the released code.

main_issue: Code differs from the Methods
finding: The main claim holds: atomic context raises recovery near ligands, most near metals. Three of six headline numbers match. The authors' own per-protein data show that the figure used a different neighbourhood definition than the Results text, and metal-only context on the metal split; that choice moves the metal number by about 15 points.

main_issue: New dependency release breaks the code
finding: All targets within 0.1σ, chains run to the paper's convergence criterion. The released setup no longer runs on CAMB 2.x; CAMB 1.3.6 works.

main_issue: Test split not published
finding: The released model behaves as described, but the test split was drawn without a fixed seed and never published, so the headline test error can't be re-checked.

main_issue: Test data not released
finding: All 46 values on real microscopy data match within 0.01. The noisy test images behind the main benchmark were never released.

main_issue: More compute than one home GPU
finding: All four values fall inside our 95% interval on a weighted 300k-window sample. The full test set would take about 115 days on our GPU.
